data.gender_notes: Vedantri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vedantri is a unisex name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'knowledgeable in Vedas'. The name Vedantri carries the meaning “Knowledgeable in Vedas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vedantri usually hope their child will grow to embody knowledgeable in vedas and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who has deep understanding and wisdom of Vedic scriptures.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vedantri total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Vedantri is a name that holds deep respect and recognition within the Hindu community. The Vedas are considered the oldest and most authoritative texts in Hinduism, containing knowledge about various aspects of life, including spirituality, ethics, astronomy, and more. There are four main Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda. Being a Vedantri signifies having a deep understanding and adherence to these sacred texts. The name conveys a rich tradition and an individual who embodies the wisdom and knowledge passed down through generations.
data.spiritual_significance: Vedantri is a name that represents a deep spiritual connection to the ancient wisdom of the Vedas. It symbolizes an individual's commitment to seek and understand the ultimate truth of life, which is the essence of the Vedas. The name encourages one to lead a righteous life based on the teachings of the Vedas and to carry forward this knowledge to future generations. It also signifies the pursuit of self-realization and enlightenment, ultimately leading to a higher state of consciousness and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Vedantri signifies one who is deeply rooted in Vedanta, the philosophical foundation of Hinduism. It symbolizes a quest for ultimate spiritual knowledge and self-realization.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads.

historical_references.reference:
Vedanta Sutras, written by Vyasa around 500 BC, form the philosophical foundation of Hinduism.
The Vedantri title is derived from Vedanta, meaning 'end of the Vedas' and 'knowledge' respectively.
Vedantri scholars are those who have studied and understood the Vedanta philosophy deeply.
References: ["Vedanta Sutras", "Vyasa", "500 BC"]

The Madhva philosopher and scholar, Anand Tirtha, was also known as Vedantacharya or Vedantri Anand Tirtha.
He was a prominent figure of the Dvaita philosophy, which emphasized the dualistic nature of the universe and the supremacy of Lord Vishnu.
References: ["Anand Tirtha", "Dvaita philosophy", "14th century"]

Overall, the name 'Vedantri' has transcended its traditional roots and gained a modern significance, representing a fusion of spirituality, culture, technology, and entrepreneurship.
